system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
**Buyer review — Wattlebridge Holdings.** The Seller’s “STANDARD”, “FINAL” and “agreed” labels are not evidence of Buyer approval or market practice. Review all positions. This assessment uses the supplied extracts; the underlying SPA and DD documents require verification.

| Issue | Seller’s position | What the Buyer should want | Recommendation and one-line reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001 — General liability cap** | General warranty liability capped at **20% / AUD 4.8m**. | Meaningful recovery proportionate to exposure, with separate regimes for fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities and fraud. | **Counter with a higher cap, opening at 100% of price**, subject to negotiated risk allocation; 20% could leave substantial acquisition losses unrecoverable. |
| **SPA-N-002 — De minimis & basket** | Claims must exceed **AUD 25,000** individually and **AUD 250,000** collectively; only the excess over the basket is recoverable. | Lower thresholds, a tipping basket, aggregation of related claims, and exclusions for protected claim categories. | **Counter, illustratively, with AUD 10,000 de minimis and AUD 120,000 tipping basket**, subject to DD; the proposed deductible and individual threshold materially erode recovery. |
| **SPA-N-003 — General claims time limit** | Notification within **18 months**; limitations extend to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | **24–36 months** for general warranties, distinct longer periods for other categories, and timely notified claims surviving expiry. | **Seek 36 months and reject automatic extension to all Claims**; 18 months may expire before latent issues emerge over reporting cycles. |
| **SPA-N-004 — Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title warranties share the general cap and deadline. | Separate protection for capacity, ownership of all shares, authority and absence of encumbrances; no basket/de minimis, cap at least the price, and longer survival. | **Reject the general regime; seek at least a 100% price cap and six-year contractual claim period**, checked against execution form and applicable law; defective ownership threatens the entire investment. |
| **SPA-N-005 — Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; no express fraud exception is supplied. | Express fraud/fraudulent misrepresentation carve-outs covering the Seller and persons for whose conduct it is responsible, preserving non-excludable statutory rights. | **Carve fraud out of every relevant exclusion, cap, threshold, time bar and remedy restriction**; broad boilerplate must not shelter fraudulent conduct or defeat mandatory rights. |
| **SPA-N-006 — Disclosure scope** | Blanket disclosure of the indexed data room, accounts, registers and public records. | Only matters fairly disclosed with sufficient detail to identify their nature and scope; specific warranty cross-references and a fixed, preserved disclosure record. | **Reject blanket/deemed disclosure and require a fair-disclosure standard**; mere availability or reference does not adequately identify a warranty exception. |
| **SPA-N-007 — Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by Buyer or advisers, including anything discoverable from the data room or public records. | No knowledge exclusion; alternatively, only actual conscious knowledge of named Buyer individuals, without imputation, constructive knowledge or a duty of inquiry. | **Delete; tightly narrow only as a negotiated fallback**, expressly preserving specific indemnities; “discoverable” transfers undiscovered Seller risks to the Buyer. |
| **SPA-N-008 — Bluefen consent** | Reasonable endeavours; written consent alone satisfies the condition. No final consent or evidence of satisfaction of associated conditions is supplied. | Buyer-waivable completion condition requiring effective consent under clauses 11.2–11.3, satisfaction of associated conditions and no unacceptable commercial changes. | **Require substantive satisfaction before Completion, not merely delivery of a letter**; approximately 30% of FY26 revenue depends on this relationship. |
| **SPA-N-009 — Riverlark facility** | Approximately **AUD 3.2m** outstanding; security release follows Completion. | Verified payout figure, repayment through completion funds flow as a Seller debt deduction, and effective release of all relevant security and guarantees at Completion. | **Require a controlled simultaneous payout-and-release process, with binding lender undertakings and subsequent registration evidence**; the Buyer must not acquire unrepaid debt or remain exposed to enforcement. |
| **SPA-N-010 — Employee bonuses** | **AUD 420,000** conditional completion bonuses omitted from funds flow; on-costs unspecified. | Seller bears transaction-triggered bonuses and applicable payroll tax, superannuation and other on-costs, with quantified funding and no double counting. | **Expressly allocate and include these amounts in completion mechanics, backed by an indemnity for shortfalls**; calling them a Seller matter does not prevent the acquired company bearing the liability. |
| **SPA-N-011 — Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to the SOW3 payment; AUD 180,000 recorded open, but non-payment is not independently verified and no receipt or confirmatory assignment is supplied. | Verified settlement and effective transfer of all relevant IP rights, plus protection against ownership defects, third-party claims and associated remediation costs. | **Require payment evidence and effective assignment before Completion where material, plus a broader specific indemnity outside general warranty limits**; paying the invoice alone may not establish usable IP ownership. |
| **SPA-N-012 — Export/privacy incident** | Described as preliminary and not expected to be material; access, scope, notification duties and loss remain unresolved. | Prompt investigation, evidence preservation, containment, legal assessment of applicable notification duties and Buyer oversight, with Seller-funded pre-completion exposure. | **Require investigation and remediation covenants plus a tailored indemnity; consider a completion condition if findings warrant it**; uncertainty is neither proof of a notifiable breach nor a basis to dismiss the risk. |
| **SPA-N-013 — Sandbar renewals** | Three AUD 110,000 renewals treated as ordinary-course operating costs. | Assess the **AUD 330,000 aggregate** commitment, timing, related scope, termination rights, accrual and compliance with interim operating covenants. | **Do not accept the classification without evidence; aggregate related commitments and allocate any exceptional burden expressly**; neither automatic Buyer operating expense nor automatic Seller debt is established. |
| **SPA-N-014 — Category separation** | General limitations and remedy restrictions apply to all Claims unless expressly excluded. | Clearly separate general warranties, fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, covenant breaches, price adjustments, completion obligations and fraud. | **Create an express claims-category matrix with overriding carve-outs across every relevant clause**; a broad “all Claims” provision could silently neutralise negotiated protections. |
| **SPA-N-015 — Title verification** | DD-012 share register records Harbourglass as holder of 100%. | Verify issued capital, ownership chain, constitution, options/convertibles, competing interests and encumbrances; obtain valid transfers and completion registration. | **Treat the register as evidence, not conclusive verification; reconcile corporate records and obtain title warranties and releases**; one register does not establish clean, transferable ownership of all equity. |
| **SPA-N-016 — Tax/IP open terms** | Tax and IP positions treated as settled under the general regime. | Separate tax covenant/indemnity for allocated pre-completion tax, appropriate tax warranties and statutory-period-based survival; robust IP ownership, licensing and infringement protection with risk-specific limits. | **Reopen both categories and negotiate their scope, caps, exclusions and survival expressly**; latent tax and core-IP exposures are not adequately addressed merely by applying general warranty limits. |

**Other disclosure distinctions:** On the supplied wording, the office lease requires notification—not necessarily consent—and Mossvale restricts assignment, not necessarily a share-sale change of control. Verify the complete provisions before imposing consent conditions.
=== END ADVICE ===
